chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Sa'd ibn Abi Amr al-Jallab, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any woman who spends the night while her husband is displeased with her regarding a right, her prayer will not be accepted until he is pleased with her; and any woman who perfumes herself for other than her husband, her prayer will not be accepted until she bathes from her perfume as she bathes from her major ritual impurity (janabah).'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a wife's prayer being accepted or rejected in Shia jurisprudence regarding husband's displeasure and perfume?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that marital harmony is a prerequisite for the spiritual acceptance of a wife's worship, linking domestic rights to ritual validity. The second condition regarding perfume highlights a specific nuance in Shia jurisprudence where applying scent for non-husbands is treated with the same ritual gravity as major impurity (janabah), requiring a full bath (ghusl) rather than simple washing. This underscores the integration of social conduct with personal piety in Shia scholarly tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Sa’ad Bin Abu Amro Al Jallab who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever woman is irrevocably divorced and her husband is angered upon her regarding a right, a Prayer would not be Accepted from her until she pleases him from it; and whichever woman perfumes herself for other than her husband, a Prayer would not be Accepted from her until she bathes from her perfume like she bathes from her sexual impurities’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Sa‘d ibn abu ‘Amr al-Jallab who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If a woman passes a night and her husband is angry with her because of a right to which she does not yield, her Salat (prayer) is not accepted until he becomes happy with her. If a woman wears perfume for other than her husband, her Salat (prayer) is not accepted until she washes them clean just as she takes a Ghusl (bath) because of going to bed.’”
